questions.enonce_markdown:
What do you understand by the following terms:

(i) Eutrophication

(ii) Food web

(iii) Commensalism? *(2, 2, 2 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Eutrophication** is the enrichment of a water body (pond, lake, river) with mineral nutrients such as nitrates and phosphates, coming from fertilisers and sewage. It causes a rapid growth of algae (algal bloom); when the algae die, bacteria decompose them and use up the dissolved oxygen, so that fish and other aquatic organisms die.

(ii) A **food web** is a network of interconnected food chains in an ecosystem, showing the feeding relationships between all the organisms.

(iii) **Commensalism** is a relationship between two organisms of different species in which one organism (the commensal) benefits while the other is neither harmed nor benefited. *Example:* an epiphytic orchid growing on a tree, or the cattle egret feeding on insects disturbed by cattle.

questions.enonce_markdown: State eight effects of bush burning on the environment. *(8 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. It **destroys vegetation** and the habitat of many animals.
2. It **kills animals** and soil organisms, including useful decomposers and nitrogen-fixing bacteria, which reduces biodiversity.
3. It **destroys humus** and reduces soil fertility.
4. It exposes the soil to **erosion** by wind and rain, and to **leaching**.
5. It causes **air pollution** by smoke, carbon dioxide and carbon monoxide, which contributes to global warming and respiratory diseases.
6. It destroys **crops, farms and property** (houses).
7. It reduces **soil water retention** and, by removing plants, reduces transpiration and rainfall locally, which can lead to **desertification**.
8. It destroys economic plants and **wood**, and it can cause **loss of lives**.
9. It leads to **loss of food** for herbivores and food chains are disrupted.

(Any eight.)

questions.enonce_markdown: In tabular form, distinguish between a food chain and a food web. *(6 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
| Food chain | Food web |
|---|---|
| A single, linear sequence of organisms showing who eats whom | A network of many interconnected food chains |
| Shows one feeding pathway only | Shows many feeding pathways |
| Each organism feeds on one kind of food and is eaten by one kind of organism | An organism may feed on several kinds of food and be eaten by several organisms |
| Simple and easy to draw | Complex, more difficult to draw |
| Less stable: if one organism is removed, the whole chain is broken | More stable: if one organism is removed, others can replace it as a source of food |
| Energy flows along one route | Energy flows along several routes |
